I am the last to
keep this book.
Nine conductors
wrote in it before
me. None of them
wrote about the
end. I will have
to.

C.1146.
The children dream
the same dream.
A deep place, and
a voice in it that
sounds like ours
but slower. Liesl
calls it the
Undersong.

Stood on the Podium
facing the Heart
tonight. Every
ring was humming a
half-tone flat. I
sang against it and
it bent back, for a
moment. Only for a
moment.

Orrin says the
Chord is being
learned. If it
learns the whole
Chord it will not
need us to hold it.
I do not want to
know what it will
sing then.

C.1147.
The Tuners' vote
is unanimous. The
Archive's too. The
choice is still
mine. That is the
one law we never
wrote down.

We will Rest.
The Heart goes
silent at the
fourth bell. The
city walks out
through the gates
in one night: the
Last Procession.

The Wardens will
stay. They cannot
be told the song is
over. They were
made to hear a
false note, and now
every note will be
false.

I have sealed the
last of our best
things under the
dais. The Bass
holds it. The deep
voice always did
the holding.

The four keys are
scattered: the deep
one below, the high
one with Liesl, the
others with their
guilds. Whoever
gathers them must
not sing them.

Someone has to
stand on the Podium
when the Heart
stops, to be sure
it stays stopped.
It should be the
conductor.

It will be me.

A LEGEND OF
AURELITH
for travellers who
arrive by gate or
by water.

Corvin, harbour-
master, Vesper
Quays. C. 1102.

THE GATES
Four towers, four
beams. From the
plain, walk toward
the light: every
beam stands on a
gate. Soprano N,
Alto E, Tenor S,
Bass W.

THE PLAZA OF THE
HELD NOTE
At the centre. The
Heart hangs above
its dais. Canticle
Way runs north and
south from here,
Held Note Avenue
east and west.

Mind the Podium,
facing the Heart.
It is the
conductor's. Do not
stand on it. People
do. The Wardens
have views.

THE VESPER QUAYS
Follow the glow.
The river crosses
the city under
three arched
bridges. Moor at
the stone posts,
not the lamps.

THE ARCADE OF
ECHOES
The long market
under the columns.
Everything is paid
for in echoes.
Hesper's lamps are
fair; others less.

THE STILLHOUSES
The quiet quarter.
Terraces, dark
glass, amber eaves.
If a door is shut,
they are sleeping.
If it is open,
knock anyway.

THE ARCHIVE OF
ECHOES
The tower of
shelves. Listen
first; the
Listeners will
not let you in
otherwise.

STARWARD
The domed tower.
Climb it on a
strong aurora.

THE QUIET GARDENS
Stepped terraces.
No talking. Truly.

THE CONDUCTOR'S
SPIRE
The tallest tower.
From its top
terrace the four
beams, the river
and the Heart all
line up. Go once.
Everyone should.
